system.coreAbility:
Bleeding. Let the life drain from its veins. When you inflict
a Wound with the Knife, the Entity begins Bleeding.
Place the Bleeding token next to the Entity as a reminder.
Bleeding is treated as a separate damage source, so can't
be boosted by abilities that affect a Hunter's damage, and
does not trigger Threat placement.
At the start of the Entity's turn, a Bleeding Entity
suffers 2 Resolve damage or, if it is Broken, 1 Wound
damage. Then, toss the Bleeding token like a coin. If it
shows Bleeding, the Entity retains the Bleeding status.
If it shows Whole, the Bleeding status is removed.
When the Entity restores Resolve, it also removes
Bleeding.
An Entity is either Bleeding or not. Bleeding cannot
be applied twice at the same time, and Bleeding damage
does not stack and is only inflicted once per round.
Bleeding persists if the Knife-wielding Hunter dies,
along with any passive abilities which apply while the
Entity is Bleeding, until it is removed.
system.outlook:
The Knife is the perpetual underdog. Every
warrior in every army throughout history has
carried a Knife, but they carried a proper Weapon
too. Something you can wave around and threaten
people with, something with a bit of heft behind it,
something you can hang on the wall when you come
back from the chaos. Something that means business.
The Knife wants to show those bastards that it
means business.
It's sharp. One cut will kill you. No hustle and
bluster; nothing but blood.
It's everywhere. It's in every house in the kingdom,
every pocket in the street. It's out of the shadows and
at their throats. No-one sees it coming.
And it's personal. You kill something with a Knife,
you have to want it dead. You open yourself up to
attack. You grip white-knuckled to the fucker and
stab until your arms ache. By the end, you're soaked
in scarlet. You earn your kill.
system.lies:
Outlook


The Knife is the perpetual underdog. Every
warrior in every army throughout history has
carried a Knife, but they carried a proper Weapon
too. Something you can wave around and threaten
people with, something with a bit of heft behind it,
something you can hang on the wall when you come
back from the chaos. Something that means business.
The Knife wants to show those bastards that it
means business.
It's sharp. One cut will kill you. No hustle and
bluster; nothing but blood.
It's everywhere. It's in every house in the kingdom,
every pocket in the street. It's out of the shadows and
at their throats. No-one sees it coming.
And it's personal. You kill something with a Knife,
you have to want it dead. You open yourself up to
attack. You grip white-knuckled to the fucker and
stab until your arms ache. By the end, you're soaked
in scarlet. You earn your kill.

Lies


The Knife knows that the world is out to get you.
You never wanted this to happen; maybe it's the
way you look, or who your parents were, or what side
of the river you grew up on. The odds were stacked
against you before you even drew a card. At every
turn, someone's arrived to steal what you've fought so
hard for without giving you a second thought.
You're not the aggressor, says the Knife: you're
taking revenge. Every drop of blood is justified. They
and theirs have kept you down for too long; you need
to fight back and take what you're owed. Your only
mistake was not doing it sooner.
If you win, you're a hero. If you lose, you were never
supposed to succeed. There's a comfort in occupying
the bottom rung, especially when it opens your
enemies up to retribution.
system.fears:
Some of the bearers that the Knife chooses are, in
fact, the sort of embittered underdogs it believes
them to be - but many aren't. They wear their
imagined persecution as a badge of honour and think
that, if so many people are dead-set against them,
they must be doing something revolutionary to shake
up the status quo.
The Knife is scared of not being underestimated.
Of not being hated. It doesn't want to be accepted.
It doesn't want people to think it's important, or
welcome it as a part of something larger and more
important. It can only imagine the world as a frantic
battle, and for its unceasing, spiteful aggression to
make any sort of sense, it must be under constant
attack. If it's not a victim, it's nothing.

forms.text:
Instead of inflicting Bleeding
on Wound damage only,
you inflict Bleeding when
you inflict any damage with the Knife.
forms.name: Bloody

forms.text:
In addition to the Knife?s Close attack, you
may now attack with Sharp from Ranged.
forms.name: Weighted

forms.text:
When you inflict Wound damage
with this Weapon, heal 1 Wound.
forms.name: Wicked

system.description:
The world is trying to hurt you. But you won't let it - you
won't be taken advantage of - you're sharp and cruel and
quick and clever - and the Knife is here right alongside you,
pressed into your palm, guiding you through the darkness
and chaos. You're going to show them they were stupid to
underestimate you. You're going to bleed them dry.

Choose the Knife if you want to:
Rely on your speed rather than your brawn.
Keep moving to stay out of trouble.
l Use Bleeding to hurt the Entity and support your allies

system.coreAbility: Be Ready. Stand your ground and brace for impact. When combat begins, you are Ready; when you become Broken or expend Ready, you are not. When you Guard, you become Ready again, in addition to the other benefits of Guarding. Track Ready with a dedicated coin or token. Some abilities are only active while you are Ready; others require you to expend Ready to activate them. Unless stated otherwise, expending Ready is an immediate action you can perform once on your turn.
system.outlook:
utting something sturdier than skin over the top of
your skin has been perennially popular ever since
humans discovered they can pull the fur off things
they've killed and wear it on their heads, but ramshackle
protection like that isn't real Armour. It wouldn't be seen
dead in uncured pelts these days.
Armour is expensive. If it's not, it's not Armour - it's just
safety equipment. No-one gives a shit about aprons but
everyone wants to wear the Armour.
Armour is polished steel, layered silk, lacquered wood
and hardened leather. Armour is as much the filigree
and flash as it is a physical barrier. The Armour is a
message, turning the wearer into a beacon of security and
prosperity. The Armour says: you've made it, and it wants
others to hear.
system.lies:
The Armour wants you to understand that what people
think of you is infinitely more important than what you
do or who you are. Honesty, integrity and earnestness are
all well and good but they're useless compared to letting
others bask in your glory. Everyone else is looking blindly
for the answers to questions they don't even know how to
ask, but you can show them the way.
Not that you want them to become like you, you
understand. Not that they could. You're better than these
people; you've cut through the horseshit and you see how to
play the system to your advantage. You want them in your
wake, singing your praises, carrying your kit and paying you
tithes. You are their champion, leading the fight against those
they despise, protecting that which they value. You want
them to believe they're dependent on you.
The Armour's favourite lie is of the self-made man - that
the bearer did it all themselves, that they had no unfair
advantages on their path to success, and that similar
outcomes are possible to anyone who applies themselves
with enough gumption. It laughs at the thought that
anyone helped them get to the top. It despises the idea of
luck. You don't need luck when you're this good.
system.fears:
The Armour is a shell to keep the world out. It hates
intimacy. Everyone who sees you without the Armour,
who witnesses the vulnerable human you are and not the
shining paragon you project, has leverage over you. It longs
to be as close to your heart as possible and to be the only
thing that gives you strength.
Spend long enough with it and you welcome the lies
into your life for the power they provide. Your allies
shelter behind you when the storm rolls in, and it feels
good to be impenetrable. Each time you drown out the
weak part of you inside, what little humanity remains
is made smaller and weaker, until only the image of the
Armour remains and you are left strange and empty.

forms.text: While you are Ready, when you would suffer Resolve damage from an Entity attack, you suffer 1 less damage.
forms.name: Hide

forms.text: When you would suffer Wound damage from an Entity attack, you may expend Ready to reduce the damage suffered by 1.
forms.name: Metal

forms.text: Attack with Quick or Sharp from Close (choose one when you take this Weapon; you can Reforge it (p. 155) to change to the other option). When you Take Cover or Move, become Ready.
forms.name: Silk

system.description:
It doesn't matter how you feel, what you do, or who
you are. What matters is what people think of you -
and people think you're great. You've made it. You're
a success. The Armour, layered over the fragile
human part of you, keeps you strong. You proved
them wrong, or did them proud; whichever story
serves you better. Why shouldn't they be impressed?
When the storm rolls in, why shouldn't they take
shelter behind you? Perhaps they would rather die
alone and exposed; so be it. There's plenty more
where they came from.

Choose the Armour if you want to:
Stay on your feet when under attack.
Protect and enhance other Hunters.
l Set up a defensive bulwark.

system.coreAbility:
Arm?s Reach. It?s a tiring task, but you keep the beast at
bay. Once per round during your turn, as an immediate
action, you may spend Resolve up to the amount of
Threat in your area to remove Threat from your area
equal to the Resolve spent.
system.outlook:
The Spear is, in all likelihood, the oldest man-made weapon
in existence. It has evolved from a length of wood that's
sharper on one end than it is on the other to a panoply of

polearms that defined the shape of warfare for thousands of
years. Whilst it lacks the idealism attached to the Sword or
the utility bound up in the Knife, the Spear was the weapon of
choice for the common soldier until upstart firearms arrived and
pushed it off the top spot.
The ubiquity and archaic nature of the Spear makes it
unfashionable, but the Spear doesn't mind. The Spear was there
at the dawn of time when the first humans decided that they
wanted to bring down beasts ten times their size, or to stab
someone whilst staying out of stabbing range themselves. The
Spear predates machines, structures, clothing, the written word,
language, and numeracy. The Spear has watched the rise and fall
of other pretenders - the aloof longbow, the cackling crossbow,
the spiteful warhammer - and knows that it will be here long after
the cities have crumbled to dust and the last bullet has been fired.
system.lies:
The Spear knows that the home - the hearth, the space you claim
as your own - is sacred. It wants to help you keep it sacred by
ensuring the profane - which is to say anything you decide you don't
like - is excluded by force. To breach the sacred is unthinkable,
and anyone who would even consider it should be destroyed.
"Home", of course, is a malleable concept. Home can be the house
in which you live, but it can be your church. Your town. Your nation.
Your kingdom. Wherever people who look like you exist. Wherever
people who share your ideals make a stand. When it comes to
Hollows, an entire plane of reality - as battered and bruised as it is -
can be a home, and worth defending. The Spear doesn't like to think
of itself as attacking. Anything the Spear does is defence, no matter
how pre-emptive it might seem or if it has to be carried over borders
and jammed in some poor bastard's guts to do it.
You are supposed to be here. You are entitled to occupy this
space, and furthermore, you are entitled to everything within
it. Anyone you let inside is yours to protect, but yours to use as
you will, and can be expelled whenever you please. They owe you
their life, after all.
system.fears:
The Spear is terrified of being abandoned. Although it is
very picky about who it lets inside what it considers to be
home, it knows (but would hesitate to say) that it needs others
to survive. What good is a King who is reliant on his subjects?
What good is a man who cannot protect his family with his own
strength and cunning alone?
It brags of sole mastery over its domain - of permissions granted
and contracts bestowed, of sworn oaths and kind allowances - but
dreads the day that its power is found wanting and those under its
protection are killed, or worse, decide to leave before it is ready to
let them go. The crossed spears, a symbol of barring and refusal,
are just as frequently used against those under the Spear's authority
as they are against those who stand against it.
system.description:
There is a line between us and them and across
that line is the Spear, keeping them away from
us. Protecting the sacred from the profane.
Defending right and killing wrong. The world is
trying to swallow you and those you care about,
but it'll have to go through you first.

Choose the Spear if you want to:
Support other Hunters in combat.
Manipulate Threat to control the fight.
l Dictate the flow of the battle.

system.outlook:
The Book is the latest form of an ancient concept -
knowledge, materialised, that can be shared or jealously
hoarded. What is now paper and ink was once chiselled
tablets of stone or rich pigment daubed across the walls of
firelit caves. It sees the world not as a chaotic mess, but instead
a series of rules which can be manipulated to its advantage.
The Book's violence is more subtle than that of its
companions in the Weapons' bloodstained pantheon. Every
Weapon is a tool through which humans impose their will
upon the world, and where the others may do so directly
with fire and iron, the Book holds itself above such base
matters. Violence is not only the crack of bone and tang
of blood; pure violence, unsullied by the sweat and pain of
the melee, is the subjugation of that which you deem to be
beneath you. The Book knows that everything is beneath it.
system.lies:
The Old Faith spoke of the power of words. Their
godlings possessed true names that could be used to
control them by simply being spoken aloud, and the Book
sees the wisdom in this concept. Let others grunt and strain
to make an impact; to understand something is to control it.
Absolute truth is not only possible but extant, and it lies
within the pages of the Book. Where others stumble around in
darkness, you have the intellect and the determination to pierce
the veil of ignorance and see the world for what it really is.
Not only that; when you impose structure on the world
around you, you give it a form pleasing to your eye. You
create species and periodic tables, constellations and
countries, ethnicities and social classes, heretics and saints.
Everything you see is yours to control and order with you,
bright and brilliant as the sun, at the centre.
system.fears:
The thought that the Book might be one day disproved fills it
with an existential dread. It cannot allow any part of itself to
become false; to do so would be to invalidate its entire existence.
Once conjecture coalesces into truth, that truth becomes
brittle and breakable. The stern wisdom that the Book
provides offers no quarter and permits no incursion upon its
sanctity. Those who build their foundations upon the Book's
truth are moral and sensible and good; those who offer an
alternative viewpoint are, logically (and the Book loves logic)
immoral, foolish, and evil. Genuine truths do not bend and
adapt in the presence of conflicting evidence, but instead
must be defended against deluded and malicious agents hellbent on their destruction.
It isn't stupid. It knows that, from the moment its final
page is written, any insight it offers becomes less relevant.
Contexts shift and erode. Touchstones crumble, idioms
invert themselves, and audiences die out. The Book is true
only as long as people believe it is, and that truth - the only
truth the Book can really guarantee - is at the root of its
implacable refusal to compromise.

forms.text:
When you Focus, the Entity
suffers 1 Resolve damage.
forms.name: Eldritch

forms.text:
When you Guard, an ally
may restore 1 Resolve.
forms.name: Sacred

system.description:
Words have power. If you name something, you
can know it, and if you know it, you can control it.
Speak a word aloud and the ground trembles at
your approach; the beasts of the land recoil and
cower; eyes are struck blind, muscles wither and
crops die. A chain around the neck of the world,
binding it to your will. Nothing is beyond your
comprehension and nothing is outside of your reach.

Choose the Book if you want to:
Heal other Hunters.
Control the battlefield.
l Play a support role.

system.coreAbility:
Loaded. All or nothing. The Shotgun doesn?t have Capacity
like other ranged Weapons. Instead, it is either Empty
or Loaded. At the start of each fight, the Shotgun is
Loaded: place the Shotgun token on your character
sheet with the Loaded side up. While it?s Loaded, you
can make an attack by flipping it to Empty; while it?s
Empty, you can make a Reload manoeuvre to flip it to
Loaded. You can only make attacks with the Shotgun
while it is Loaded. You may only use the sections of your
abilities matching the current state of your Weapon.
In general, effects that restore Capacity also allow you
to flip the Shotgun from Empty to Loaded.
system.outlook:
The Shotgun (or blunderbuss, or dragon, or
scattergun, or coach gun) uses a sizeable charge
to fire multiple projectiles at a target. On the upside,
the spread of shot means that accuracy is no longer a
concern - on the downside, the laborious process of
loading the ammunition leaves the bearer vulnerable to
attack once they've pulled the trigger.
It is not a new or complicated concept. Whilst
the Rifle and Pistol have made recent advances with
regards to accuracy, capacity and rate of fire, the
Shotgun has been perfectly happy to blast great clouds
of debris downrange for centuries with very little
change in its construction. It is easy to make, easy to
use, and you can fire pretty much anything out of it
and still make an impact.
It is immediate and indiscriminate violence in physical
form. It promises absolute destruction at the pull of
a trigger: an attack without patience or restraint that
sends even the fiercest foe reeling.
system.lies:
What if, the Shotgun asks, you no longer held
back? The world is a web of carefully-maintained
social constructs designed to hold our baser impulses in
check and, not coincidentally, keep power in the hands
of those who already possess it. The game is rigged
from the start, but you don't have to play it. There's an
advantage in being the wild card, and to ignore all the
restrictions and boundaries placed upon you. To do the
unthinkable. To kill and maim and ruin.
Certainly intimidation and fear have their place, but
that's not what the blood-hungry Shotgun is interested
in. It wants action. It wants to blow the world clean
in half and relish in the aftermath. It wants to break
things to prove that they can be broken. Violence is the
only form of communication that matters, and you've
got the ultimate solution to any given problem: death.
system.fears:
Death is not the ultimate solution to any problem.
The Shotgun knows this.
Those carefully-maintained social constructs can't
be torn asunder so easily. The Shotgun doesn't like to
think about what happens after the shot is fired and
the smoke clears; that it is empty, and powerless, and
open to retribution.
It hates being unloaded, and it hates not being fired.
What it desires is impossible and intoxicating: no
waiting and no need for recovery, but only an endless
instant of fury. It exists solely for that brief moment of
fire and noise and the fleeting taste of absolute power.
The lies it tells are wild and unsustainable, but to the
right person, they'll hold together long enough.

from Ranged with the Shotgun.
forms.name: Long-Barrel

to Empty, toss the Shotgun token
like a coin. If it shows Loaded, it?s
Loaded; if it shows Empty, it?s Empty.

forms.name: Sawn-Off

system.description:
There are things out there that want to kill you - terrible
things, wretched things, bestial things. You're not scared
of them. They should be scared of you. You're mess and
you're chaos, you're indiscriminate, you're a massacre
waiting to happen. There's nothing you can't kill, nothing
you can't break, nothing you can't ruin.

Choose the Shotgun if you want to:
Cause plenty of damage.
Enhance your abilities with clever positioning.
l Get more powerful the more danger you're in.

system.coreAbility:
Terribly Calm. Slow is smooth, smooth is fast. You may
hold up to 5 Focus. Discard all your current Focus when
you become Broken or enter Support. Unless you have
abilities which state otherwise, you still begin each battle
with 0 Focus.
system.outlook:
The Rifle conquered the world. When the dominion
of the Isles was at its height, it was at the heart of
every conquering force: trade and diplomacy may be
what cements an empire in place, but violence digs the
foundations. The Rifle was the perfect tool for the job:
accurate, reliable, and deadly. The long barrel and heavy
charge of gunpowder let soldiers engage with the enemy
at a respectable distance - no swirling melee, no barbaric
brawling, but a measured march towards victory. With a
Rifle, you can kill a man and never see the fear in his eyes,
or smell the stench of death, or hear the last breath stutter
staccato out of his foaming mouth.
But one Rifle doesn't win a war; ten thousand Rifles
do. To deliver ten thousand Rifles - and the ammunition
needed to fire them, and the tools to maintain them, and
the spare parts to swap out during a campaign, and the
soldiers to carry them - you need infrastructure. You need
steel refineries and weapons manufacturers and cargo ships
and iron ore mines and anti-union laws and strikebreakers
and vassal nations and bloodlines and flags and the
continual threat, whether implied or explicit, of absolute
violence against those who disagree with you. You need
civilisation.
The Rifle is the foremost, sharpest point of the grand
machine that was the empire.
system.lies:
Stand up straight and walk tall - you've earned it. A life
of hard work and good decisions, backed up by the
hard work and good decisions of your forefathers, sets
you apart from the rest. You've earned your money, your
comfort, your security.
You are untouchable, unimpeachable, unflappable. You
can do whatever you want because you are in charge and
whatever you want is the right thing to do. Those who think
differently to you are weak, immoral, bestial, petty, deluded.
Things instead of people.
You're the conquering army. You're the state. You're the
rules. You're the boys' club, the back-room deal, the secret
handshake, the right choice made at the right time with the
right people. You cannot be stopped.
system.fears:
What use is a Rifle without bullets? What happens when
the sights misalign, when the mechanism jams, when
the bolt sticks in the chamber or the powder's too wet to fire?
It's just dead weight to carry around - an obligation you've
brought upon yourself and that you're too proud to forsake.
The Rifle is scared of being unsupported and alone -
away from supply lines, from convenience and comfort,
from those it deems peer or peon. It knows that, if left
alone and told to manifest its destiny, it's dead in the water.
It needs everything underneath it ticking like clockwork to
even survive.
system.description:
The world is dangerous but you are more
dangerous; you are the apex predator. You are
calm; you are methodical; you are operating far
above your base instincts. There is no wilderness
or threat that you cannot tame or kill. The land
is rotten and corrupted but you, paragon of
patience, stand pristine above it all.

Choose the Rifle if you want to:
Attack at range.
Be accurate, dangerous and methodical.
l Inflict Wound damage to finish the battle
decisively.

system.coreAbility:
Flourish. Show the beast that you mean business. Once
during your turn you may place 2 Threat on your area to
Feint as an immediate action. Feint is a special action only
available to Sword-wielders.
system.outlook:
The Sword is the King of Weapons. Ancient empires
rose and fell at its point. For millennia, the Sword has
been a symbol of power and authority beyond measure:

a tool for the masters of men to wield with skill and
grace. To cut away the weakest parts of society and to do
what must be done to ensure civilisation's survival and
prosperity.
Fate coalesces around the Sword's point. The Sword
makes myths. It rests in stones waiting for someone
deserving of the honour to rule the kingdom. It severs the
heads of tyrants and rests upon the right hands of great
men. It can elevate a common citizen to knighthood with
but a touch.
Next to the Sword, the frantic fear of the Knife and the
Spear fall away to nothing. The brutish Bludgeon falters
and stumbles. The Book is cut to shreds, the Staff sliced
in twain, the Armour rent asunder and the sound and fury
of the firearm silenced. It gladly bears the burden laid
upon its shoulders - someone's got to do it. Someone has
to lead the charge.
system.lies:
The Sword believes in heroes in the ancient sense of
the word. It wants to convince its wielders that they
stand proudly ahead of their peers: that there are those
who are born to lead, thanks to some indefinable spark of
greatness deep within their being, and it is their duty to
shepherd the people beneath them.
But the glorious ages of the past have died. The world
has grown sour and corrupt, and the concepts of which
the Sword sings - honour, duty, nobility and sacrifice -
are twisted and withered things. It spits hate on the
feckless masses and preaches exceptionalism. It tells you:
you alone are meant for greatness. These pitiful creatures
are nothing without you to lead them. You are worthy of
the respect you see glinting in their bovine eyes.
system.fears:
The Sword's time in the sun is over, and it clings to
what little relevance it retains. As the rifle and the
field gun scar the globe into new and terrible empires, the
Sword sees their eyes on the throne. It feels itself slipping
into rite and ritual as it becomes a relic of bygone days.
The Sword only matters if the people know it matters. Its
authority is not innate, but granted with conditions. Spears
outreach it. Knives carve and craft and make. It glances off
Armour's skin and every single gun outranges it.
So it speaks of honourable combat. It admonishes those
who fight dirty and births schools of duellists, manuals
of techniques, and reams of rules designed to fashion
the grim business of ending lives into something that
demands admiration and grace. It is desperate to dictate
the battlefield and hold onto its unfair advantage, because
without it, it is nothing but a length of sharpened steel.

forms.text:
When you Feint, your Sword damage
increases to 3/3 until the end of your turn.
forms.name: Mighty

forms.text:
When you Feint, one Hunter in your
area may Guard as an immediate action.
forms.name: Noble

forms.text:
When you Feint, one Hunter in your
area may Focus as an immediate action.
forms.name: Short

system.description:
There are fighters and there are warriors and you,
friend, are a warrior. You are a professional. You
have earned the right to lead an army, to seize the
reins of civilisation, to cut and stab and kill. In
your hand is the Sword, the tool of a master, and
the key to victory. Show them what you can do.

Choose the Sword if you want to:
Support and lead other Hunters.
Inflict reliable damage.
l Be adaptable and dynamic.

system.outlook:
The Pistol is chief amongst the new gods of bloodshed;
gunpowder and lead put a lightning strike in the
palm of the everyman, and almost every hero of every
story now clutches a handgun at some point in the tale.
Where clergymen would bless swords, they now pray
over pistols and ask the gods to guide the shooter's hand.
Advertisements on street corners and the back pages of
periodicals boast of skull-cracking strength, quick-draw
designs and affordable ammunition.
The Sword has been replaced as a mark of personal
prowess - no longer do you have to train for years to use
a weapon, or risk your skin by coming close to those you
want to hurt. Anyone with a few quid and a vendetta can
set the odds in their favour with a Pistol in their pocket.
system.lies:
The Pistol tells you: you're the best there is. No-one
has what you've got; you're unique, and special, and
fascinating. The world is chaotic and unfocused but you,
Pistol gripped against your skin, rise above the noise and
move unfettered.
A lack of success or prosperity should be no indication that
maybe you've overestimated yourself; instead, it's everyone
else's fault that you've not made it yet. Your ideas are too
new, too revolutionary, to be accepted. Anyone who passes
you over or looks down on you knows the truth: they're
jealous of your ability and scared of what you might do.
This absolute refusal to change based on new
information brings with it a bullet-proof confidence, and
the Pistol wants to propel its bearers forward into the
future on the back of it. Reality is what you make it, and
you're the guy holding the gun.
system.fears:
Ignore the flash and the posturing. The Pistol believes
that it isn't supposed to be here, but as long as no-one
else finds out, it's fine. It's fine.
It's not an instrument of war; no great glories, no stern
sacrifices, no tactical masterstrokes owe it thanks. It's not a
tool for hunting, either; thick hides turn aside little bullets,
rifles outrange it, and it's a coward's crutch next to the cut
and thrust of finishing the beast with blade and bludgeon.
It's not a part of anything greater, or ancient, or more noble.
No abstraction or artifice masks it with the sacrosanct.
All it does is kill people. Is that enough? Is the Pistol
enough?
It spins stories of its own prowess and whispers feverish
in the ears of those who carry it: you're the best, you're
the greatest, you're streets ahead of these fools. It keeps
everyone and everything at arm's length. It never shows
an ounce of weakness or confusion if it can help it. The
alternative is unthinkable; a crash and burn, a dethroning,
and a cold eternity of exile. Better to keep up the act
forever than run the risk of discovery.

system.description:
You're strong. Smart. Capable. The world's set against
you but with the Pistol resting on your hip or howling
in your hand you can weather any storm. You're a force
to be reckoned with, and those fools will be left in your
wake when you show them what you can do.

Choose the Pistol if you want to:
Attack from range or up close, whatever's best.
Power up when you inflict Wound damage.
